author: Suzette Lowe FOR JACKSON NEWSPAPERS
title: New gym and entrance highlight Ripley Middle Phase I improvements | Jackson Star and Herald - Ripley and Ravenswood | wvnews.com
text:
RIPLEY, W.Va. – Neither verbal descriptions nor photos can quite prepare anyone for the completed renovations and new construction at Ripley Middle School.
For Assistant Superintendent for Non-Instructional Services Tim Brown, who served as the school's principal for over 16 years, this project is a little personal.
“Ripley Middle was my second home,” he said. “And we needed these changes badly.”
During a tour of the school given by Brown, there were countless additions and changes to point out and explain.
The most obvious was the new gymnasium, a complete addition to the school. One of the most striking features is the murals at each end of the facility.
“The Viking mural is massive and made with 96 vinyl panels,” Brown said. “It looks like wet paint to me, because it’s so shiny and almost seamless. The ‘Home of the Vikings’ design was taken from the 3-D ones I had bought as principal. They don’t make those anymore so that we couldn’t replace them.”
The bleachers seat 900 and are retractable, and the baskets are movable so that the gym can easily be used for volleyball.
“The scoreboards are huge, but they look small in comparison to the space,” Brown said. “In fact, the whole gym looked small to me for a long time. I’d say that to Tommy White (clerk of the works who oversees the construction). Then, when the ceilings went in, it changed the whole perspective.”
Moving from the gym to the lobby and the new school entrance is just as impressive, including the unique lighting.
Certain areas can be blocked off during games but give extra space during the school day.
There are new trophy cases and student seating with charging ports. New team locker rooms are separate from the physical education ones.
With televisions in the lobby and at the concession stand, no one will have to miss the game if they’re waiting on food or serving.
The foyer in the new school entrance may be as far as most parents have to come if they’re signing out their child.
“There is a window there and seating to wait,” Brown said. “The child will just meet them there.”
There are two things that Brown is very happy with in the design plan.
“There is a lot of storage which is very much needed,” he said. “And parking, especially once we get the back area completed, is a game changer. Ultimately, we will have around 300 spots, up from the 60 we’ve had.”
This year, teachers will have to park in a portion of the new parking lot, which is also used for student drop-off and pick-up. But Brown said it will be an improvement over last school year.
The bus lane can accommodate four wide and six long vehicles, and vehicle drop-offs also have a spacious area. Students will enter the new gym from the drop-off area.
With a new front office, an elevator for special needs, new administrative and finance secretary offices, and a new stairway leading to the 8th grade wing, Phase I of the multi-million dollar renovation is nearly complete.
“The challenge, at least for the next few months, is getting from the new wing to the classrooms in the original building,” Brown said. “It’s not connected yet, but is under construction. So we’re forming a path with a double construction fence that will be monitored.”
While Brown said the plan isn’t ideal, it’s the best option for now.
“Kids are resilient,” he said. “I don’t think we’ll hear much complaint from them, and we’ll determine how much time they need to get from one area to the other after they settle in.”
There are four phases for this project.
- Phase I was the administration offices, locker rooms, elevator, and gymnasium
- Phase II is underway with demolition of the old gym, which will become the new cafeteria and kitchen, and connecting the new and old wings
- Phase III will be the STEAM room, which will be located in the current cafeteria; a wall will be built that will separate that present-day open area from the adjacent classrooms
- Phase IV is a refresh of the 6th grade wing, which is nearly finished
“The new cafeteria, when completed, can still be used for sports practices,” Brown said. “The kitchen area will be twice as big as the one there now. The old kitchen will be classrooms. The only two areas that we didn’t put in the plans, and I honestly don’t know how we missed it, are the teacher’s lounge and the staff restrooms.”
There is one addition to Ripley Middle that Brown hopes will never be used.
“We’ve got a tremendous fire suppression system,” he said. “The water pressure the city can provide would not be enough. But this is something we hope we will never have to utilize.”
The Ripley Middle School project was chiefly funded by the West Virginia School Building Authority ($13,547,398), with some matching money ($6 million) provided by the board of education. The contractor is United Construction, with ZMM Architects and Engineers as the architectural firm.
